knowledge_point.title: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2}$ means that we need to swap the first and second rows.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 5 & 2 \\ -1 & 5 & 4 & 1 \\ 3 & 7 & 1 & 9\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3}$ on $M?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5 & -1 & 2 & 1 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3}
$$

$$
\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 5+(-1)(5) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(-1) & 1+(-1)(1) \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]}
$$

$$
\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 9 & 1 \\ 0 & -3 & 3 & 0 \\ 5 & 2 & -1 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

knowledge_point.title: Applying Row Operations To an Augmented Matrix

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{1}:=2R_{1}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{1}:=2R_{1}$ means that we need to multiply the first row of the matrix by $2.$

Multiplying the $1$st row by $2$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 2 & 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}:=2R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2\cdot 1 & 2\cdot 2 & 2\cdot 3 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}2 & 4 & 6 \\ 3 & 4 & 5 \\ 4 & 6 & 7\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}R_{1} &\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ R_{2} &:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation $R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{3}$ means that we need to swap the first and third rows.

- The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the third row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}-1 & 9 & -2 & 6 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ 9 & 0 & 5 & 7\end{array}\right]\,R_{1}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4 & 4 & 6 & 7 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{3} \\ &\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 4+(-1)(-1) & 4+(-1)(9) & 6+(-1)(-2) & 7+(-1)(6) \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}9 & 0 & 5 & 7 \\ 5 & -5 & 8 & 1 \\ -1 & 9 & -2 & 6\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $M,$ given by

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ on $M?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the third row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
M=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1 & -1 & 1 & 2\end{array}\right]\,R_{3}:=R_{3}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}
$$

$$
\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & -1+(-1)(0) & 1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(3)\end{array}\right]}
$$

$$
\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & -2 & 1 & 4 \\ 0 & -1 & -1 & -1\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $U,$ given by

$$
U=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $U?$

$$
\begin{aligned}R_{2} &:=\frac{1}{2}R_{2} \\ R_{3} &:=R_{3}+(1)\cdot R_{2}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation $R_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}R_{2}$ means that we need to multiply the second row of the matrix by $\frac{1}{2}.$

- The operation $R_{3}:=R_{3}+(1)\cdot R_{2}$ means that we need to add $1$ times the second row to the third row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}U &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 2 & 0 & 6 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=\frac{1}{2}R_{2} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & -1 & -3 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{3}:=R_{3}+(1)\cdot R_{2} \\ &\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0+(1)(0) & -1+(1)(1) & -3+(1)(0) & 4+(1)(3)\end{array}\right]} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 2 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 \\ 0 & 0 & -3 & 7\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $A,$ given by

$$
A=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}R_{3}$ on $A?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}R_{3}$ means that we need to multiply the third row of the matrix by $-\frac{1}{3}.$

Multiplying the $3$rd row by $-\frac{1}{3}$, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}A &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ 6 & -3 & 9 & 0\end{array}\right]\,R_{3}:=-\frac{1}{3}R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ -\frac{1}{3}\cdot 6 & -\frac{1}{3}\cdot (-3) & -\frac{1}{3}\cdot 9 & -\frac{1}{3}\cdot 0\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 8 & -1 \\ 7 & 1 & -9 & 4 \\ -2 & 1 & -3 & 0\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $T,$ given by

$$
T=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(2)\cdot R_{1}$ on $T?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(2)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}T &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2 & -2 & 1\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(2)\cdot R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 2 \\ -2+(2)(1) & -2+(2)(3) & 1+(2)(2)\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & 3 & 2 \\ 0 & 4 & 5\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $X,$ given by

$$
X=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ on $X?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
X=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & 5 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}
$$

$$
\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & 5+(-1)(3) & -1+(-1)(2) & 2+(-1)(1) \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right]}
$$

$$
\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 0 & 2 & -3 & 1 \\ 3 & 4 & -2 & 3\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $N,$ given by

$$
N=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-2)\cdot R_{1}$ on $N?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-2)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-2$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
N=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-2)\cdot R_{1}
$$

$$
\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 2+(-2)(1) & 1+(-2)(-2) & 2+(-2)(1) & 3+(-2)(-1) \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right]}
$$

$$
\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & -2 & 1 & -1 \\ 0 & 5 & 0 & 5 \\ 7 & -1 & 3 & 1\end{array}\right]
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $V,$ given by

$$
V=\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the following row operations on $V?$

$$
\begin{aligned}R_{2} &\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ R_{2} &:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}\end{aligned}
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Let's list the required operations:

- The operation $R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3}$ means that we need to swap the second and third rows.

- The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-1$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying the operations, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}V &= \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 1 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 3\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}\leftrightarrow R_{3} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1 & -1 & 0 & 3 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 1\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-1)\cdot R_{1} \\ &\sim {\scriptsize \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 1+(-1)(1) & -1+(-1)(0) & 0+(-1)(0) & 3+(-1)(2) \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 1\end{array}\right]} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}1 & 0 & 0 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & 0 & 1 \\ 4 & 3 & 2 & 1\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Consider the augmented matrix $B,$ given by

$$
B=\left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right].
$$

What matrix results from carrying out the row operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)\cdot R_{1}$ on $B?$
question.:question/worked-solution:
The operation $R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)\cdot R_{1}$ means that we need to add $-3$ times the first row to the second row.

Applying this row operation, we obtain the following:

$$
\begin{aligned}B &= \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3 & -4 & 4\end{array}\right]\,R_{2}:=R_{2}+(-3)\cdot R_{1} \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 3+(-3)(1) & -4+(-3)(-1) & 4+(-3)(2)\end{array}\right] \\ &\sim \left[\begin{array}{cc|c}1 & -1 & 2 \\ 0 & -1 & -2\end{array}\right]\end{aligned}
$$
